title: Personal Checking: identifying the item that opened a negative episode
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to the bank-error review of the most recently posted extended overdraft fee on a Personal Checking account. It identifies, where the record allows, the item that opened the negative episode on which that fee was charged.

## Formal clause

The item that opened the episode is identified through the account's most recently posted overdraft item fee:

- when that overdraft item fee posted exactly the tier's extended overdraft trigger period, in calendar days, before the extended overdraft fee, it posted on the day the episode began, and the item named as its source item opened the episode;
- otherwise the opening item is not identified, and only the amount ground is judged.

## Input, judgement, output

```
Most recently posted overdraft item fee  ->  its posting date
Reviewed extended overdraft fee          ->  its posting date
Calendar days between the two dates equal to the trigger period?
     Yes -> the overdraft item fee's source item opened the episode
     No  -> opening item not identified; only the amount ground is judged
```

## Boundary cases (hypothetical trigger period of 10 calendar days, extended overdraft fee posted 2026-07-21)

| Most recent overdraft item fee posted | Days before the extended fee | Opening item |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-11 | 10 | Identified: that fee's source item |
| 2026-07-12 | 9 | Not identified |
| 2026-07-09 | 12 | Not identified |
| No overdraft item fee on the account | — | Not identified |

(The trigger period of 10 days is chosen only for illustration.)

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "any overdraft item fee in the episode points to the opening item". **Correct basis:** only the most recently posted overdraft item fee is used, and only when it posted exactly the trigger period before the extended overdraft fee.
- **Wrong reading:** "when the opening item cannot be identified, the extended fee is refunded to be safe". **Correct basis:** only the amount ground is then judged.
